findings.title: A backup code can be used without the account password
findings.body: Password verification is skipped whenever the request contains any truthy `totpCode` (lines 121-129), before this new backup-code branch selects the second factor. A caller can therefore POST a valid `backupCode` together with an arbitrary nonempty `totpCode`; the bogus TOTP is never validated because the backup branch is selected, and the password is never checked. The UI normally retains the password from the first step, but the credentials endpoint is directly callable, so a stolen recovery code becomes a standalone login credential rather than a replacement only for the authenticator factor. Establish and verify the first factor independently of the user-controlled factor-selection fields, or reject simultaneous factor fields and require a password/pre-authentication proof for this flow.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic, allowing recovery-code replay
findings.body: The code reads and validates the decrypted list, then later writes a separately encrypted replacement list without any conditional update, lock, or transaction. Two concurrent authorization requests can both read the same valid code before either update, both pass validation, and both return authenticated sessions. Concurrent use of different codes can also cause the last writer to overwrite the other writer's consumption, leaving an already-used code valid again. Consume the code with a compare-and-swap/conditional update on the previously read value or a transaction with appropriate row locking, and only authenticate when that update succeeds.

findings.title: Dismissing the backup-code screen can leave enabled 2FA unreported to the parent
findings.body: After the enable endpoint succeeds, this only switches to the backup-code step; `onEnable` is deferred until the dedicated `backup-codes-close` button is clicked. The outer controlled Dialog has a separate `onOpenChange` close path (line 166), so closing it through its normal dismiss controls such as Escape, overlay, or close button does not call `onEnable` or reset state. The server has already enabled 2FA, but the settings parent can continue showing its stale disabled state; if the modal is unmounted, the one-time display of the newly generated codes is also lost and setup cannot be rerun because 2FA is already enabled. Prevent dismissal while this step is shown or handle every post-enable close path by notifying the parent and preserving/acknowledging the codes.

findings.title: The feature has no automated test of backup-code authentication or one-time use
findings.body: The added coverage only verifies that the backup-code download button emits a download and that Copy shows a toast; it explicitly leaves the file/clipboard contents unchecked and never logs out and signs in through the Lost access path. Consequently the core new behavior—accepting a generated code, rejecting an invalid code, and rejecting the same code after successful use—is untested. Add an end-to-end or integration test that obtains a generated code and verifies those authentication and consumption semantics, including concurrent/conditional consumption behavior.
